cbssports.com/nba/news/luka-doncic-yaxel.headline: Luka Dončić teaches Yaxel Lendeborg a lesson, but Warriors bail their rookie out in comeback win over Lakers
cbssports.com/nba/news/luka-doncic-yaxel.author: Brad Botkin

paragraphs.text: Oct 31, 2026 at 12:25 pm ET • 4 min read

When Yaxel Lendeborg decided it would be a good idea to start a war of words with Luka Dončić during and after his first career NBA game, basically calling the Lakers superstar a flopping crybaby for whom he "lost all respect," both Stephen Curry and Steve Kerr had the same message for their brash rookie.
"Now you've got to back it up."

Friday night was Lendeborg's chance to do just that when the Warriors hosted Dončić and the Lakers for the start of the NBA Cup's group stage. It did not, to put it politely, go well for Lendeborg, who laid down the worst track of his young career with six points, one rebound, zero assists and five turnovers.
Why Yaxel Lendeborg could be the key to saving what's left of the Warriors' Stephen Curry era

Lendeborg got into early foul trouble and was never a factor on either end. For a guy who has injected so much juice into what looked like an old, disinterested, almost lifeless Warriors team when it faced these same Lakers on opening night, Lendeborg was all but invisible in finishing as a game-low minus-20 in his 24 minutes before fouling out.

When asked what lesson he had taken from a performance like this after shining such a spotlight on himself with the Luka comments, and what he might do differently next time, Lendeborg, with the same brutal honest he has shown at every turn, said he would "try not to wet the bed as bad as I did."

Meanwhile, Dončić -- who was egging on the "Luka sucks!" chant coming from the Chase Center crowd early on -- poured in 21 first-quarter points en route to 37 for the game. He added seven rebounds, five assists, a pair of blocks and a steal for good measure. He outscored the entire Warriors team in the first quarter by himself as the Lakers raced out to a 25-point first-half lead.

Certainly everything you've read so far would suggest the Lakers ran away with this game, but in today's NBA, a 20-point lead is just prologue for a second-half plot twist. And sure enough, the Warriors, behind eight 3-pointers and 31 points from Curry, stormed back to win going away, 112-95, for their third straight victory after opening the season 0-3.

Lendeborg might not have been able to back up his Dončić talk (which, we have to point out, was nothing but the truth, even if you could argue he would've been better off keeping it to himself, at least this early in his career), but the greatest shooter to ever set foot on this planet had his back. This is how you go at Luka Dončić ...
And this ...

It wasn't just Curry -- who passed Dominique Wilkins for 18th on the NBA's all-time scoring list -- coming to Lendeborg's rescue. It was Brandin Podziemski with 21 points, six assists and five rebounds. It was De'Anthony Melton and Georges Niang tag-teaming for 27 points and seven 3-pointers. It was Draymond Green taking over the Dončić defensive duties and dishing out nine dimes. It was the Warriors' bench outscoring L.A.'s bench 50-7, and a defense that held the Lakers to just 57 points over the final three quarters to fuel an astounding 42-point turnaround.

For Lendeborg, there's a lesson here that goes beyond not riling up a superstar and letting your play do the talking (which, I will restate, was fine; he's a grown man, and he didn't say anything that everyone else doesn't think), which is that it ultimately doesn't matter that Dončić got the better of him individually on Friday, because in the end it was the Warriors that got the better of the Lakers.
This was the message that Kerr had for Lendeborg after the opener in which Lendeborg was all too proud of his individual defense on Dončić.

"He did a good job on Luka one-on-one, but we got torched by Luka as a team," Kerr said. "All those stats that the NBA puts up, like, 'Hey, when he guarded him, who the eff cares?' It's like, they scored 127 on us. That stuff's all bulls---. It's our defense."

Translation: it's a team game. As his career progresses, Lendeborg, a clear alpha, is going to be the one picking up his teammates on plenty of nights, but on this night it was the rookie who needed his teammates to cover for him. Suffice it to say, they did that, and Lendeborg, to his credit, recognized the effort with genuine humility.

"Them boys had my back today," Lendeborg said, noting that in his effort to stay calm and not let the hype of the matchup take over, he actually stayed "a little too calm" and never got into a groove. "Steph Curry, again, did his thing. The bench mob showed up today. It was awesome. They all played a great game. I feel like I was the only Debbie downer on the team. I feel like next time I get into one of these games, just try to be that guy sucking up all the energy."

engadget.com/2300259/why-spotify-uses-so.headline: Why Your Spotify Might Be Using So Much Storage
engadget.com/2300259/why-spotify-uses-so.author: Adnan Ahmed

paragraphs.text: If you're running low on storage, it's worth checking to see if Spotify might be the culprit.

We're all getting tired of subscription-based services, but when it comes to music streaming, it's a little harder to give up. You can still purchase individual tracks and albums, but it's often more economical to subscribe to Apple Music or Spotify if you listen to a wide variety of music. Furthermore, with how fast and reliable mobile data has become, you can stream virtually any song you want on the go. This saves you the hassle of managing a local library of music on your phone, not to mention the storage space you could otherwise use for other apps and media files.

If you've recently been hit by the low-storage warning on your phone, you can find out exactly what's taking up so much space. On iOS, navigate to Settings > General > iPhone Storage. If you're using Android, the exact menu labels may vary depending on your phone's manufacturer, and the easiest way to find this information may be to simply search your phone for "Storage." For Samsung, look under Settings > Device care > Storage. For other Android devices, you can usually locate it under Settings > Storage or Settings > About Phone > Storage. Your phone might automatically sort your apps by how much storage they're occupying. If you spot Spotify near the top, there's a good chance that downloaded music or cached data is what's eating away at your phone's storage.

Android lets you clear an app's cache in just a few taps. Navigate to something like Settings > Apps > See all apps > Spotify > Storage & cache and tap on Clear cache. Though you can nuke your entire offline music library by tapping on the Clear storage button, this will also sign you out of the app. Instead, the Spotify app offers a much better way to manage your downloads.
Manage your Spotify downloads

In the Spotify app on Android and iOS, you can check what music you have downloaded by navigating to the Your Library tab and tapping on Downloaded at the top. Here, you can pick individual playlists or albums and tap on the green download button to remove them from your device. This is a good way to free up storage by deleting the songs you don't want available offline, while keeping the stuff you do listen to more frequently.

You can, however, delete all downloads if you want to reclaim as much storage on your phone as possible. In the Spotify app, tap on your profile picture in the top-left corner of the screen. Navigate to Settings and privacy > Data-saving and offline, scroll all the way down and tap on Remove next to the Remove all downloads option. You can also clear Spotify's cache here.

You might need to restart your phone if you don't immediately see the freed-up storage reflected in your phone's settings. Other streaming services like Apple Music and Netflix also let you remove downloads — you just have to look for the option within the app's settings.

If you're using the Spotify app on a Windows or macOS computer, you can clear downloads by clicking on your profile picture, navigating to Settings, scrolling all the way down to the Storage section and clicking on Remove all downloads. Those who use Spotify on the web shouldn't have to worry about downloads taking up device storage, since the browser version doesn't support offline listening to begin with.
Adjust media quality on Spotify

If you do need an offline music library so you can listen to your tracks without an internet connection, you can still clear some storage space by adjusting the quality of your downloaded songs. On Android and iOS, launch Spotify and head to Settings and privacy > Media quality and scroll to the Download quality section. You can choose the Low option, then tap on the Download button next to the Update existing downloads option. Spotify says tracks downloaded or streamed in the Low quality setting are equivalent to around 24 kbps, which shouldn't be too bad for casual listening.

It's also worth noting that if you have the Lossless quality preset selected for your downloads, your offline music library is going to occupy significantly more storage. Lossless tracks are much larger than their compressed counterparts. While lossless audio can upgrade your music listening experience if you're using wired headphones and a DAC, the difference might not be noticeable if you usually opt for wireless earbuds.

I tested just how big of a difference downloading the same set of songs in different quality presets can make. With my music library downloaded in Lossless quality, Spotify was occupying around 22GB of space on my phone. When set to the Low preset, my entire music library fit in a little over 2GB — those are massive storage savings, and I didn't even have to give up offline listening. Periodically clearing Spotify's cache can also free up a noticeable amount of storage space.

thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6186144-ol.headline: Olivia Rodrigo gives Amy Acton flowers at Columbus concert
thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6186144-ol.author: Ford McCracken

paragraphs.text: Pop star Olivia Rodrigo delivered flowers to Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton (D) during her tour stop in Columbus on Friday night, a show of support in the close contest.
While performing her song “stupid song,” Rodrigo walked through the crowd at the Schottenstein Center on The Ohio State University’s campus, handed flowers to Acton and embraced her.

During her first show in Columbus, Rodrigo wore an “Amy Acton for Governor” shirt, showing her support for the Democratic nominee who is locked in a competitive race against Republican Vivek Ramaswamy.
“Ohio loves you,” Acton wrote on the social platform X, with an image of Rodrigo wearing the campaign shirt.
Ramaswamy drew controversy for running an ad featuring Acton’s estranged mother, who calls her daughter a “liar” and says she is unfit for office.

Acton’s stepfather was charged with sexually abusing Acton at a young age, and Acton was removed from her mother’s custody at age 12. Acton’s mother stayed with their stepfather until his death, the campaign said.

The ad prompted blowback from both parties, including Ohio’s current Republican governor, Mike DeWine, who said the ad should be taken down. Ramaswamy’s campaign put millions behind airing the ad statewide, but it recently came down after running its cycle on the air.
Nonpartisan election forecaster Decision Desk HQ, a partner of The Hill, gives Acton a 61 percent chance of beating Ramaswamy.

Rodrigo has supported political causes in the past, namely reproductive rights. After a leaked draft opinion of the Supreme Court’s ruling in Dobbs v. Jackson, Rodrigo called out the decision at one of her concerts.
“I couldn’t pass up the opportunity to talk about how heartbroken I am over the Supreme Court’s potential decision to overturn Roe v. Wade,” Rodrigo said at the concert.
The singer recently raised $20 million for women’s health at an August benefit concert.

And when the Trump administration posted social media videos of Immigration and Customs Enforcement raids using Rodrigo’s music, she condemned the move and later told NPR that she thinks the administration is baiting pop stars into a response.

cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-c.headline: Binance says 90% of $6.3 billion hack losses are now covered, plans to resume withdrawals Sunday
cnbc.com/2026/10/31/binance-hack-asset-c.author: Michael Wayland

paragraphs.text: Binance said Saturday that it has covered up to 90% of the roughly $6.3 billion in token assets stolen from its hot wallets in a record crypto theft announced Thursday.
Binance said it will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens.
"All BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB, SOL, USDC, XRP, USD1, RLUSD, and ZEC are fully backed 100%," Binance said in a statement. "Binance will absorb the financial impact of these stolen funds, not our users."
The exchange said the outstanding 10% consists of tokens outside its top 10 that are "less liquid, which means they may take longer to source in the required amounts."
Binance said it is tapping its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), a portion of its Futures insurance fund, and its corporate treasury to replenish the assets.

"Our commitment remains the same: Binance will fully cover the financial impact of the funds stolen in this incident. We will continue to demonstrate this commitment through measurable progress, transparent reporting, and concrete actions," Binance said.
Its "next milestone" will be resuming withdrawal services for users by Sunday, subject to security checks, while the exchange continues its investigation into the attack, it said.
Binance did not immediately respond to CNBC for additional details or updates on its investigation.
It still isn't clear how the attack — the largest crypto theft on record — took place.

The world's largest crypto exchange initially said the hack may involve "a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." However, Co-CEO Richard Teng later said the attack involved a more complex process rather than the misuse of a single engineer's permissions.
It also wasn't clear who was responsible for the breach. But TRM Labs, a blockchain intelligence and AI investigations company, pointed to North Korean hackers as the potential culprits.

"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst," the company said.
— CNBC's Jenny Lee, Liz Napolitano and Davis Giangiulio contributed to this report.

sports.yahoo.com/articles/brad-keselowsk.headline: Brad Keselowski granted release to explore NASCAR rides, will sell stake in RFK Racing

paragraphs.text: MARTINSVILLE, Va. (AP) — Brad Keselowski has been granted permission to pursue other NASCAR opportunities for the 2027 season and will sell his 20% equity stake in Roush Fenway Keselowski Racing.

Keselowski announced a month ago that he was leaving the Cup Series team he joined as a driver, competition executive and part-owner five years ago, but he had been restricted from exploring rides with other teams despite his driving contract expiring after the 2026 season. He said the team granted him a verbal release Saturday, an hour before his news conference at Martinsville Speedway, and he is allowed to drive for any team or manufacturer in NASCAR next season.

“I’m ready to be elite for the next opportunity, whether driver, owner or manager,” said Keselowski, who read from a prepared statement before taking questions. “There are a number of opportunities in front of me in the Cup series for 2027 and beyond. I’ve had a number of outreaches. I’m not going to get into the details of what those are at this time, but I’m eager and willing to execute one of them and to be a part of the 2027 season as a manager and a driver.
“Now that I’ve been granted the release, I can meaningfully engage in the opportunities that exist. I was more or less taking phone calls and unable to do much with them.”

Keselowski wants to remain in the Cup Series but said he also would be open to racing full time in the Craftsman Truck Series, which would give him a shot at becoming the first champion in NASCAR’s top three national series.

He has some longtime ties with Dodge, which reentered the truck series with its Ram brand this season and is mulling a move into the Cup Series next year. Keselowski won the 2012 Cup championship with Dodge in the manufacturer’s most recent season at NASCAR’s premier level. His late father, Bob, also had a Dodge-affiliated truck team.
Keselowski has driven the past 14 seasons for Ford with Team Penske, and RFK and said he would consider driving for any manufacturer next season.

“I have not had a meaningful discussion with Dodge or Ram,” he said. “I’m certainly very open-minded to it. I haven’t given up on continuing a relationship with Ford, along with Chevrolet and Toyota. Everything’s on the table right now.”
Keselowski said he was confident of continuing a NASCAR national series career that began in 2004.
“But there’s a level of uncertainty for sure,” he said. “Nothing comes easy in this sport. We’re going to have to grind really hard to get a deal done for next year.”

Keselowski has 36 Cup victories, most recently at Darlington Raceway in May 2024. He has only six top-10 finishes in 34 starts this season but believes he can still be a winner in NASCAR as a driver, manager and team owner.
“To not be able to race would be devastating to me,” he said. “This is my life and career. I’m not ready to be done.”

nytimes.com/live/2026/10/31/world/france.headline: Thousands Expected to Protest in France on Halloween: Live Updates
nytimes.com/live/2026/10/31/world/france.author: Mark Landler, Ségolène Le Stradic, Ségolène Le Stradic, Catherine Porter, Leo Sands

paragraphs.text: Paris5:34 p.m. Oct. 31
Latest
Mark Landler and Ségolène Le Stradic
Here is the latest.

Hundreds of thousands of protesters were on the streets in cities across France again on Saturday, a now-weekly expression of national grievance that has led to clashes between protesters and the police, and kept the country on edge.

Adding to those fears: Halloween, which also falls on Saturday. The French authorities, citing calls on social media for people to revolt that encouraged them to wear masks and costumes, warned that the risk of a new outbreak of violence was high.

In Paris, tensions began flaring between protesters and the police in the late afternoon, as officers fired rounds of tear gas at people who refused to disperse. The Paris police estimated that 70,000 people marched in the demonstration in the city, compared with 110,000 last Saturday. The interior ministry estimated that nationwide, 320,000 people had demonstrated, compared with 410,000 last week. Protesters and the police also clashed in Marseille, Lyon, Toulouse, and Rennes.

Earlier in the week, France’s interior minister, Laurent Nuñez, promised to deploy 70,000 police officers, matching the numbers on Oct. 24. That operation helped keep a lid on outbreaks of arson and looting, although then, too, there were clashes as the police tried to disperse the crowds in the evening.

There was ample fuel for a repeat of those combustible scenes. Students, who are returning to school on Monday after a two-week break, were not mollified by the government’s initial response to their demands. The Education Ministry agreed to cap some class sizes, offer low-interest loans to rebuild school buildings and phase out an unpopular online college admissions platform.

The students vowed to go on protesting. Their two-month-old movement has grown to include university students, public workers and veterans of the “yellow vest” movement that convulsed France from 2018 to 2020.
The authorities have said they are most worried about trouble breaking out after nightfall.

“We are seeing numerous calls to gather coming from the far left, the radicalized extreme left, and from certain radicalized ‘yellow vests’ websites, which are urging people to attend rallies or public gatherings starting at 8 p.m. in many cities across France,” Mr. Nuñez said at a news conference.

Some of the messages were violent, Mr. Nuñez said, calling for “revolution” and “insurrection.” Those gatherings will be forbidden, and any attempt to gather in spite of the ban will lead to arrests, he said.

Demonstrators have been encouraged on social media to turn up wearing Halloween costumes. Mr. Nuñez warned it was a criminal offense to conceal one’s face during a demonstration in which public order is disrupted.
Here’s what else to know.

• Social media: French officials are increasingly concerned about the role played by social media in attracting people and inciting them to violent behavior. Speculation that the government considered temporarily suspending several popular sites drew a denial from President Emmanuel Macron himself. Read more ›

• Far-right activists: While the government has blamed far-left activists for much of the mayhem, officials confirmed that bands of young men with links to the far right have also infiltrated the demonstrations. They use the pretext of protecting shop owners but often end up in clashes with far-left groups.
• Widening movement: The nationwide unrest in France began with a handful of student demonstrations at high schools in suburban Paris last month. Read more ›

Tensions are now flaring between protesters and the police in Paris. Police are firing rounds of tear gas at people, who are refusing to disperse. The Paris police estimated that 70,000 people marched in the demonstration, compared with 110,000 last Saturday.
The Interior Ministry estimated that 320,000 people took part in protests across the country today. That is somewhat fewer than last week (410,000) and the week before (550,000).

The demonstration in Paris remains peaceful, even festive. But police and protesters have clashed in Marseille, Lyon, Toulouse, and Rennes. Tear gas and water cannons have been deployed as the police try to disperse crowds. Violence typically breaks out at the end of these rallies, when people refuse to leave the scene.
Ségolène Le Stradic
I am walking along the authorized route for the demonstration in Paris. For the most part, the mood has been festive. Someone even dropped candy from his balcony, drawing cheers from the crowd.

After, I watched a half-dozen protesters dressed in black and wearing masks push trash bins in the middle of the crowd. One was already burning as they made their way, and they set the second on fire not far from where a police unit was stationed. Other demonstrators used water to put out the fire, causing a small clash with the ones wearing in black. “That’s no way to protest,” one of the demonstrators who put out the fire said.

The protest in Paris has a joyous and playful atmosphere. Brass bands are playing music, and many protesters have come dressed in Halloween costumes. Many said they wanted to help reverse the narrative set on Oct. 17 when riots spilled out of marches across France, leading to destruction and looting.

“I’m really worried about how the riots have been instrumentalized by the far right,” said Helen Olive, 50, who was among a group of parents who came dressed as “super parents.” “We want to turn that narrative around.”

Literature student Arthur Fleury, 20, arrived as a prisoner riding a dinosaur and wore a mask of the far-right politician Marine Le Pen. “Protests are about making demands but also having fun,” he said. “I was going for an absurd costume to capture the spirit of the movement.”

Early estimates from the French interior ministry suggest crowds are smaller today than the past two Saturdays. At 2 p.m., the ministry estimated that 15,000 people were taking part in 65 protests. That compares to 37,000 people last week at that time and 67,000 on Oct. 17. These numbers can be expected to grow as the day progresses. The ministry said it had arrested 27 people, compared with 217 by this time last Saturday. Protest organizers have yet to issue a crowd estimate; their numbers are typically far higher.

I’m at the Place de la Bastille. It is normally a bustling square, particularly on a beautiful, sunny Saturday. Now, police officers with shields and helmets patrol in groups. A loudspeaker blares a warning that gatherings and protests are forbidden to take place here by a police decree and that anyone who breaks it will be fined 135 euros.
Union and student organizers had again hoped to start their march here today, and again it was denied by the police and moved to the eastern edge of the city.
French officials eye social media’s role in promoting unrest.

As France prepares for another round of protests, officials have grown increasingly concerned about the role played by social media in attracting people to demonstrations and inciting them to violent behavior.
Speculation that the government considered temporarily suspending several popular sites drew a denial from President Emmanuel Macron himself.

But in an interview on YouTube, Mr. Macron said that social media platforms would be required “to remove illegal content, and to be very vigilant about the use of certain features to prevent them from being misused by people who want to engage in looting or other such activities.”

That followed a report by a left-leaning online news site that Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu had sent a letter to leading telecommunications operators, asking them to be prepared to block Snapchat, TikTok and Instagram. Mr. Lecornu’s office declined to comment on the authenticity of the letter.

Of the four reported recipients, one did not respond to questions and two declined to comment. A spokesman for the fourth, Orange, the only one in which the state is a shareholder, declined to confirm that a letter was received but said that “like any other operator, we are required to comply with the obligations legally imposed on us by the competent authorities, in accordance with applicable law.”
How a small student movement spread across France.
The nationwide unrest in France began with a handful of student demonstrations at high schools in suburban Paris last month.

Now, in cities across the country, antigovernment marchers are protesting expensive living conditions, high fuel prices and conditions in schools. Using the unrest as a smoke screen for vandalism, rioters and looters have also joined in.
With the protests in their second month, the police have arrested thousands, and politicians are divided over how to respond.
Here is a breakdown of what has happened.
Protest in a Parisian suburb

Soon after returning from the summer break, students at a high school in the working class Parisian suburb of Créteil staged a protest, according to videos posted to social media on Sept. 18. The high schoolers objected to inadequate resources and high workloads.

Within days, students elsewhere around Paris initiated similar demonstrations. At schools in the capital’s poorest suburbs, students blocked entrances to protest crumbling infrastructure, overcrowded classrooms and what they say are flaws in the admissions system for higher education.
Demonstrations spread across France
By Sept. 29, the unrest had spread to around 400 schools around the country, according to rally organizers.
The union of high school students said the blockades were a protest against a “lack of teachers and staff, dilapidated schools, overcrowded schedules and classrooms.”
Students barricaded the entrances to some schools with obstacles including e-bikes, while others threw projectiles and set fire to trash cans.

The French education minister, Édouard Geffray, said that some of the students’ demands were “legitimate” but condemned the confrontational nature of their protests. He said that students had chased teachers and targeted school principals with firework-launching tubes.
By the end of September, nearly 80 people had been injured, and the authorities had detained more than 440, including many minors.
University students bolster the movement

Within days, the number of schools engulfed in the protests had doubled. According to the Interior Ministry, by Oct. 2, they had spread to more than 1,000 schools across France, including 220 that were blockaded. University students also began taking part.

Around this time, the authorities said that the protests were mutating from legitimate expressions of educational grievances into something more dangerous, accusing people of shooting mortar-style fireworks, burning public buildings and looting.
By Oct. 2, nearly 400 police officers and over 230 school employees and students had been injured. The number of arrests climbed to 3,000.
The movement broadens
The actions widened in October to encompass labor unions, parents and other activists, as different grievances converged into a mass protest.

On Oct. 6, around 256,000 people marched through Paris and 40 other French cities, according to the Interior Ministry. A union of high school students said protesters had occupied some 1,800 high schools.

The protests were mostly peaceful, but a fire was ignited in Lyon, and police officers used tear gas, including in Paris. The total number of arrested rose to 6,000, the authorities said. A major union of French judges and prosecutors and a human rights group accused the police of using disproportionate force, including against children as young as 14.

Two days later, on Oct. 8, smaller demonstrations were staged throughout the country, rallying around 71,500 people. The following week, the Interior Ministry said that 160,000 people joined marches on Oct. 13 across France.
The largest demonstrations yet

More than half a million people joined 110 antigovernment marches throughout France on Oct. 17, according to an official estimate. A major union, the C.G.T., put the number even higher, at 800,000. Using either count, it was the largest day of protest since the demonstrations began in September.

Many of the marchers were peaceful, but some were not. Around the country, rioters vandalized around 1,500 shops, the authorities said. In Paris, where over 100,000 people marched peacefully, a few hundred rioters faced off against officers. According to the police, the rioters burned cars and smashed storefronts.
In the large town of Limoges, in central France, rioters set fire to the 19th-century City Hall. In a moment captured on video, the building’s spire collapsed in flames.

marketwatch.com/story/how-to-use-i-bonds.headline: Want guaranteed income in retirement without an annuity? Try laddering I bonds.

paragraphs.text: How to use I-bonds to create inflation-proof income in retirement
Your retirement savings need to keep up with inflation, and Series I bonds are designed to do just that.

The interest rates for Series I bonds reset every six months, on Nov. 1 and May 1, and at times when inflation is rising, these announcements become news events. However, if you're using I-bonds the way they were intended, as an inflation hedge, it shouldn't matter that much to you. Each year, no matter what, you'd be buying a set dollar amount - up to the $10,000-a-year limit for each Social Security number - and then letting it ride.

That's what Scott Cederburg has been doing for the past five years, in a very tortoiselike approach that he calls setting up his own "retirement annuity." It actually goes against his nature: Cederburg is a 44-year-old professor of finance at the Eller College of Management at the University of Arizona, and his best-known piece of research involves putting 100% of a retirement portfolio into stocks. He not only studies this, he also practices it with his own retirement funds, which are split between U.S. and international funds.
"All of my retirement is 100% equity," said Cederburg. "I think of the I-bonds as a supplement to Social Security. That's real income."

His game plan is to keep putting away $10,000 a year in I-bonds for the next 20 or so years, until retirement. He buys the bonds from TreasuryDirect.gov once a year, a 10-minute task he doesn't think about again until it's time to buy again the next year. When he started this process in 2021, the fixed rate on I-bonds was 0% and the inflation rate was minimal. He wasn't making much in terms of interest, but he wasn't losing ground, either.

For the rate that lasts through Oct. 31, the fixed part is 0.90% and the annualized adjustable inflation rate is 3.34%, for a combined six-month rate of 4.26%. TipsWatch.com, a website from journalist David Enna that closely watches rates on Treasury products, predicts the rate announced for Nov. 1 will be a fixed rate of 1.4% and an inflation rate of 4.08%, for an annualized combined rate of 5.51%. If the fixed rate is 1.3% instead, the annualized combined rate would be 5.41%, Enna noted.
Either way, that rate is attractive compared with all the other options on the market right now, like CDs, high-yield savings accounts or short-term Treasurys.

But that's beside the point, really. The strategy for I-bonds is a long-term one. It's an inflation hedge for savings, not a way to chase yields. And that's exactly why Cederburg compares it to an annuity and doesn't even consider it part of his investing portfolio, which is invested quite aggressively.
The endgame with I-bonds

What matters most about I-bonds, if you save consistently over the years, is how you plan on withdrawing the money. Cederburg does not have a spreadsheet or software to plan out this process. He keeps it very simple: right now the money is going in, and later he will start taking it out. What he likes about I-bonds versus, say Treasury inflation-protected securities, is that you don't have to worry about redeeming at a particular maturity date.

If you buy TIPS directly from the government, you have to buy them in durations of 5, 10 or 30 years. If you buy maturity-based exchange-traded funds, you can build a ladder of the intervening years, but that means that each year, you have to commit to a certain amount coming due. The same goes for CDs or Treasury bills, bonds and notes, which don't have built-in inflation protection but do have maturity terms.

You can cash in I-bonds once you pass the one-year maturity lock-in. If you sell within five years, you lose three months of interest payments, but after five years, you are free to cash them in at any point at full value plus growth. You can also choose which I-bonds you cash in, so you have a lot of control. They reach full maturity after 30 years, after which they no longer earn interest. You pay federal ordinary income taxes on the interest upon redemption, but that interest is exempt from state and local income taxes.

"Once you get into retirement, you can choose which I-bonds to take out," said Cederburg. "At that point, it's optimal to take out the ones with the lowest rate. I have some at a zero percent fixed rate. I'd take those out first. If they raise the fixed rate on Nov. 1, that might be a bond that I hold onto longer."

Cederburg locked onto I-bonds because he was studying inflation and found I-bonds to be the best option for fixed-income savings. They beat TIPS for simplicity, ease of use, taxation and sometimes on rates. They also beat annuities on inflation protection. "Some annuities are suited to protect you from longevity risk, but a lot of annuities are not inflation protected. You get a set dollar amount a year, but it doesn't guarantee you buying power with that," he said.

While $10,000 may not sound like an enormous amount of retirement savings, it will add up over time. If Cederburg maintains this strategy for 25 years, he'll have $250,000 in principal, plus growth that equals the inflation rate. He has assured purchasing power. He can then start taking out money. If he ends up with a balance of around $400,000 at age 65, he could create an income stream for 30 years that is around $2,000 a month.
Not bad for 10 minutes of work a year. "From my perspective, that's the nice thing about it. Set it once and forget it, and come back 20 years later," Cederburg said.

techcrunch.com/2026/10/31/openai-reporte.headline: OpenAI reportedly lowers funding target for new round
techcrunch.com/2026/10/31/openai-reporte.author: Anthony Ha

paragraphs.text: OpenAI’s latest funding round isn’t quite living up to expectations, according to multiple news reports.

OpenAI was previously reported to be raising $30 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation, and then at a $1.25 trillion valuation, ahead of a planned IPO. But The Financial Times reported Friday that the company has subsequently lowered its funding target to $20 billion, with a first close that’s expected to be even lower than that.

The round will be led by a group of investors from the United Arab Emirates, the FT said. A subsequent retail offering for wealthy individuals could bring the total funding amount to the $20 billion target.

A follow-up story in The Wall Street Journal offered more details, namely that the company has secured $11 billion so far, and that its fundraising efforts had met with a “tepid” response from some large investors.

TechCrunch has reached out to OpenAI for comment. The company’s reported funding challenges could be blamed, in part, on bad timing, as Wall Street investors have become wary of heavy AI infrastructure spending, leading to a major sell off of tech stocks. And Anthropic’s planned IPO could be facing challenges, too.

engadget.com/2301242/how-long-should-usb.headline: How Long Is Too Long For A USB Cable?
engadget.com/2301242/how-long-should-usb.author: Robin Bea

paragraphs.text: One of the best things about USB is that you rarely need to think about it. Sure, there are some differences between USB generations, but no matter what, if you plug a USB cable into a compatible device, it will work without issues, as long as the cable isn't too long, that is. Of course, you're unlikely to need an extremely lengthy USB cable — unlike, say, HDMI cables — but if you ever do, there are limits to USB cable length that you should be aware of.

The USB Implementers Forum (USB-IF), which defines USB standards, has outlined maximum lengths for different types of USB cables. These range from about 16 feet to as low as 3 feet. The Forum is an industry group, not a regulatory body, so there's nothing stopping manufacturers from making longer cables. The limits are a guide to best practices, as exceeding the USB-IF's specifications could hamper a USB cable's performance.
USB transfer speeds suffer with longer cables

Each generation of USB cables can transfer data faster than the last, but later generations actually have a shorter recommended length. USB 1.0 and 2.0 cables have a recommended maximum of 16.4 feet. For USB 3.0 through 3.2, that drops to 9.8 feet. USB 4 cables are much more limited, with a maximum recommended length of just 2.6 feet. Whether you're using a USB-A or USB-C cable doesn't matter; the maximum length is the same either way.

It might seem odd that maximum cable length doesn't improve over time as transfer rate does, but it has to do with the physical limits of the cables. A signal traveling through a cable degrades over time due to electrical resistance. The farther a signal has to travel, the more cable it has to push through to get there, losing signal along the way. Longer cables are also more susceptible to damage, which can further slow transfer speeds.

A USB cable that's too long won't suddenly stop working. Instead, it simply won't function as well as one that's within spec. Data may transfer more slowly than you're used to, or connected devices won't receive as much power. The higher the potential transfer rate or power delivery, the more you're likely to notice the difference. That's why it's important to know the maximum length of your USB cables.
How to extend the range of a USB cable

If you can, it's always best to reposition your devices so you don't need to exceed a USB cable's length limits, but that's not always possible. In those cases, you can purchase an active USB cable or an active USB extender, either of which will have built-in components to extend the signal's range. However, active USB cables are significantly more expensive than standard cables. They also draw extra power from the USB port, and thus might not be compatible with older ports.

Another potential solution is to use a powered USB hub and use the longest supported cable between the hub and your computer. Plugging too many devices into the same hub can slow them down, but as long as you don't exceed the USB port's bandwidth, you shouldn't encounter any noticeable performance difference. Powered hubs are preferable, since an unpowered hub can only draw power from the USB port, which can be unreliable.

sports.yahoo.com/articles/amol-muzumdar-.headline: Amol Muzumdar hints at specialist T20I squad for India women: 'Not long'

paragraphs.text: Indian women's cricket team have been excellent in Test and ODI formats in recent times. Under former captain Harmanpreet Kaur, they won four of their last five Tests, a big feat considering that only four countries play Test cricket in the women's game. They are also the reigning Women's ODI World Cup champions, having clinched their maiden title almost exactly a year ago.
However, their T20I game still needs improvement. India were knocked out in the league stage of the 2024 and 2026 T20 World Cups. In the shortest format, the team needs to improve on many fronts.

Head coach Amol Muzumdar believes India could soon have a specialist T20I squad, similar to the men's team, with the next generation of cricketers better equipped to meet the demands of the format. Asked how soon that could become a reality, Muzumdar replied: “Not long.”

“We’re already on that path. There’s some amazing talent coming through. The talent I’ve seen at the CoE (Centre of Excellence), where they hold the India Under-15 and U-19 camps, is terrific. The work at the CoE is superb. The camps are a good reflection of where Indian women’s cricket is at the moment. I’m sure it’s in a healthy state,” he said at an event organised by the Sports Journalists’ Association of Mumbai (SJAM) at the MIG Club on Saturday.

Muzumdar believes the next generation could speed up that transition. Having grown up with the demands of modern T20 cricket, these players have a better understanding of the importance of nutrition, fitness and fielding.

“They are tuned in. They are professionals. Even the U-15 players are professionals. They understand the nutrition aspect of the game. They understand the fitness aspect of the game. They understand fielding. They’re terrific fielders. They’re good athletes. They understand that athleticism is key in cricket. You’ll soon find that when the younger generation takes over, India will be in a good state,” he said.

The coach also said that a player's willingness to learn was as important to him as their skill. “I see whether he or she is receptive. If he or she is receptive, you know it from their body language. You need to learn to understand the body language of the player. Over the years, I have spent a few years in First-Class cricket, and I do understand that I can know a certain player through their body language on the ground. I try to catch those signals. There is always that correct timing of that advice that has to be given. So as a coach, you need to understand when to say, how to say and what to say,” he felt.

Muzumdar said he was also conscious of giving players the space they needed. “Sometimes you have to respect the space that the athlete wants. You can have 10,000 things as a coach to tell that athlete. But whether he or she is in that time frame or the mind frame to understand what you are doing...” he said.

A year after India won their maiden Women's ODI World Cup title, beating South Africa in the final at the DY Patil Stadium in Navi Mumbai on November 2, Muzumdar recalled the team spirit that marked the campaign. He credited the unity within the squad and the atmosphere in the dressing room for helping the team during the tournament.

“If I have to pinpoint just one, then I think the unity in the camp and the dressing room atmosphere. Because of that unity, the dressing room atmosphere was very light. There was a little bit of a buzz around in the dressing room, which I love to create,” he said.
Muzumdar compared that atmosphere to the Mumbai teams he played for in the 1990s, which won the Ranji Trophy several times during that period.

“I have played in such teams where whenever we have done well, what I am talking about in the 90s, when we did well, just the dressing room atmosphere was phenomenal. There was some kind of a buzz triggered to the kind of cricket that was reflected on the ground. So I think if I have to pinpoint one, it is unity in the camp and just the buzz in the dressing room,” he said.
Having worked closely with Harmanpreet during his three-year tenure, Muzumdar praised the outgoing captain and said he was looking forward to working with new skipper Smriti Mandhana.

“I had a very good time with Harman as a captain. But I’m also looking forward to the future. With utmost respect, the manner in which she conducted herself as a captain, as a skipper, was superb. I feel myself really lucky that I had that opportunity for the three years that I spent with her as a coach. I could gather the mindset of the captain... I could gather the mindset of the leader in her. I consider myself really lucky about it,” he said.
Muzumdar said he wanted to build a culture of dominance and ruthlessness on the field in the Indian women's team.
“Dominance is something that we have always spoken about within the squad. Being ruthless on the ground is another thing that we have always maintained. I don’t know where it stems from,” he said.
Much of Muzumdar's coaching philosophy comes from his formative years in Mumbai cricket. The former domestic stalwart said he wanted to pass on those lessons to the Indian women's team.

“Obviously, from the background where I come, the kind of majority growth in Mumbai cricket was similar. I try to inculcate those things or give it back. If we start dominating world cricket, I would be happy.”

Differences in FanDuel Racing odds vs. sportsbook odds

Parimutuel odds are used in horse racing, which means that every bet goes into a pool of money, and the odds change based on what percentage of the money is placed on each horse. That means that the odds can change after you make a wager. For example, a horse might be 20-1 at the window when you place your wager, but if money rolls in late on that horse, it might be 10-1 by the time the race begins.

Because all the wagers are pooled, payout odds will be exactly the same regardless of what race book you're using. That's different than in sports betting, where your odds are locked in at the time of your wager and may vary from book to book. That stark contrast is by far the biggest difference between betting on horse racing and betting on sports.

If at any point you do not like the latest odds, you have the option to cancel your horse racing wager, as long as the race has not begun, for a full refund. One exception to this is futures pools, where all bets are final. A futures pool is where you try to predict the winner of a big horse race weeks or months before it.

FanDuel Racing's My Stable feature and handicapping store

Tips and advice for betting on horse racing

Not all handicappers have the same preferences, but information is key for betting on horse racing. Speed figures, recent performances, running style, training times and dozens of other factors can all help inform your decision-making. Weather is also a crucial factor in horse racing, with different track conditions often favoring certain styles of runners or horses who have had relevant experience.

Understanding the competition that a horse has competed against and how he's improved over time can also help give you insight into making winning horse racing picks. It's a sport steeped in tradition with thousands of data points, and you can use that data to develop a strategy that you're comfortable with. You can also mitigate risk with concepts like dutching (betting multiple horses to win the same race) and the 80/20 rule (80% of your stake on place and 20% on win).

Regardless of your strategy, though, it's important to remember that there are a lot of variables baked into horse racing. You should only wager what you're comfortable losing. It can be entertaining to be longshot wagers like trifectas and Pick 4/5/6's, they're low probability wagers, and you should manage your bankroll carefully. Betting outside of your means or chasing losses can spiral quickly.

Pakistan won its first multi-nation title in the 1985/86 season, when it won both the John Player Triangular Tournament in Sri Lanka and the Austral-Asia Cup in the UAE. Over the next three decades, the team became the most reliable tournament side in neutral conditions, particularly in Sharjah.

ODI success for Pakistan has come in three forms, namely ICC and Asian Cricket Council events, multi-nation tri-series and cups, and two-team bilateral series. The four titles at the top level are the 1992 World Cup, the 2000 Asia Cup, the 2012 Asia Cup and the 2017 Champions Trophy, while the rest of the list is made up of tri-series and bilateral wins.

The wait could end soon, as Pakistan are due to meet Sri Lanka in the final of the ODI tri-series in Lahore. The former state Senate president, who unsuccessfully ran for governor this cycle, replaced progressive oyster farmer Graham Platner on the ticket when Platner’s bid imploded amid sexual misconduct allegations. In a state that went to Vice President Harris in the 2024 presidential election, Collins is leaning on her seniority and stressing her distance from Trump — particularly on tariffs, which have strained Mainers’ pocketbooks and caused problems with Canada, a vital trading partner that shares a 600-mile border with the Pine Tree State.    Democrat Adam Hamilton, a Methodist pastor and former Republican, has put Sen.

“If Democrats win Kansas, not only is it winning a state that they haven't won in a Senate race since 1932, the longest such drought in the country for either major party, but … for the Senate control question, it gives Democrats sort of an additional card to play,” he said. “If they were to win Kansas, maybe they don't need to flip Iowa.   But neither candidate was polling past 50 percent, opening up the possibility that the race kicks into a second round of ranked-choice tabulations.

Maine is the only other state with ranked-choice voting statewide.   The Trump administration filed a lawsuit in late October seeking to block certification of the Senate election if the incumbent loses with Daniel J. Sullivan, who goes by Dan Sullivan, also on the ballot.

engadget.com/2303277/nasa-second-year-lo.headline: NASA's Second Year-Long Mars Simulation Mission Ends Today
engadget.com/2303277/nasa-second-year-lo.author: Mariella Moon

paragraphs.text: The agency will livestream the event starting at 3PM Eastern time.

The second set of volunteers for the Crew Health and Performance Exploration Analog (CHAPEA) mission is exiting NASA's mock Mars habitat after 378 days. NASA will stream the event live on YouTube and on its social media accounts, starting today at 3PM Eastern time. Ross Elder, Matthew Montgomery, Ellen Ellis and James Spicer entered the habitat on October 19, 2025, as part of the CHAPEA mission 2 crew.

They lived inside a 3D-printed 1,700-square-foot facility on NASA Johnson grounds in Houston, Texas for over a year, conducting Mars mission operations right here on Earth. They did simulated spacewalks, performed habitat maintenance and grew plants. The crew even has to go through an airlock to leave the habitat. In addition to the isolation, the participants were subjected to other stressors future spacefarers to Mars and the moon would face, like communication delays and resource limitations.

NASA started looking for volunteers for the CHAPEA missions in 2023, and the first crew entered the habitat in June that year. The agency has already started accepting applications for the Moon and Mars Exploration Analog for another year-long experience that combines elements of CHAPEA with NASA's other space simulation experiences. That mission will begin no earlier than August 2027. NASA says data from the missions can help it optimize food system design for its future lunar missions and prepare for the other aspects of spending long stretches of time in space.
100-meter water resistance for use in water sports

This watch had the rigid resin case, but with 100-meter water resistance. Its comfortable fit and lightweight design made it great for swimming and other water sports, and it also had a stopwatch, timer, and other functions useful for athletes. Even powering all this functionality, the battery life was still great, at about five years.
First calculator-style Casio watch

This wristwatch incorporated a keypad the user could operate with a fingertip, leveraging original Casio miniaturization technology. In addition to doing all you would want in a watch, it offered all four arithmetic operations to eight digits. Even further, the Finger Touch System (FTS) circuitry could electronically determine the likely intended key when the user pressed two or more at once. Reinterpreting accidental input to grasp what the user meant to do — this was a truly conscientious design touch of the sort only Casio, a calculator maker, would think of. This timepiece was a milestone in both multifunctional watch development and wearable calculator design.
Jogging watch with pace-setting function

This sports-oriented timepiece was created just in time for the worldwide jogging boom. Helping joggers keep their desired cadence with an electronic signal, the watch could also measure required time, distance, number of steps/strides, and average speed if the user specified stride length. It also displayed lap times down to 1/100 of a second. Rigid resin was used to allow for a lightweight, colorful design. From athletic-minded younger fans to health-conscious older users, joggers of all ages loved this watch.
Digital watches with English-Japanese & Japanese-English dictionaries

Casio leveraged original LSI technology to develop a CPU capable of running English-Japanese and Japanese-English dictionaries on these digital watches. The T-1500 included English terms and phrases at about the level of a junior high school graduate, while the T-2000 went further with terms and expressions for travelers and businesspeople. Needless to say, all the desired basic watch functions were included, as well. Another new step for Casio — a “walking dictionary” that changed the time-telling wristwatch into a wearable information device.
Diver’s watch with 200-meter water resistance

Designed to perform as a diver’s watch, this was the first Casio digital watch to deliver 200-meter water resistance. The stainless-steel, screw-lock case back ensured a water-tight seal. Paired with a top bezel made of resin, this made for an all-around heavy-duty design. Even when using the stopwatch or timer functions, the watch also separately displayed the current time, a highly practical feature. More than ready for intensive use, it also had long-term stamina, with a battery life of around seven years.
First wristwatch with a built-in thermometer

The TS-1000 could tell the temperature, another first for a wristwatch. It employed a fine ceramic semiconductor called a thermistor to sense changes in temperature. The alarm function even notified users of temperatures above or below specified ranges. Despite the greater number of components, the watch was still an easy size to wear, thanks to the new single-chip microprocessor and high-density mounting technology. This also ensured low power consumption, providing for a roughly three-year battery life.
AQ-500 (Janus)
First Casio analog-digital combination watch with three hands

Offering both a digital display and an analog display complete with hour, minute, and seconds hands, this watch gave the advantages of both: an intuitive grasp of the time at a glance and confirmation of the time with precision. The name was inspired by Janus, the two-headed god of time from ancient Roman mythology. It boasted a refined design to complement dressy, formal attire, along with functionality like a stopwatch and dual time display. Variations including a gold version and one with a leather band were offered to meet users’ increasingly diverse needs.
AT-550 (Janus Read Sensor)
Touchscreen watch ahead of its time

This watch not only boasted a streamlined design combining analog hour, minute, and seconds hands with digital LCD, but was also equipped with a calculator function allowing manual input. Users could draw numbers and math symbols with a fingertip on the glass, and the LCD would then display the formulas and calculation results. This epoch-making watch is still known as one of the first watches with the kind of gesture recognition people use today on smartphones and smartwatches. Not bad for the early ’80s.

The technical achievement was significant. The touch sensor incorporated a transparent terminal switch as the cover-glass of the watch face. The originally developed Finger Trace Recognition System (FTRS) provided character recognition architecture that delivered accurate results regardless of factors such as the size of the letters or where characters were traced on the screen. This was a true pioneer in wristwatch multi-functionality requiring no physical buttons.
Calculator watch that could perform scientific calculations

The CFX-200 added full-fledged scientific calculator functionality to the C-80 calculator watch which, three years earlier, already had a keypad allowing direct fingertip input and 8-digit calculation functions. Offering support for 25 scientific calculation functions, 12 types of unit conversions, and memory for three fixed numbers, this amazing tech breakthrough met a broad range of needs, from research to practical work. It was a truly high-spec timepiece, boasting an abundant selection of practical features for daily life and business settings as well, with stopwatch and alarm functions, 12/24-hour format switching, and more.
DW-5000C (G-SHOCK)
Tough watch that overturned common sense about the wristwatch

The very first G-SHOCK hit the scene at a time when people thought of wristwatches as sensitive instruments in need of careful handling. Turning this conventional thinking on its head, the G-SHOCK created all-new value by redefining the timepiece as a tough tool that could withstand drops and impacts. The development story began with a single-sentence proposal to construct a tough watch that would not break even if dropped. After about two years of trial-and-error and over 200 prototypes, Casio finally achieved a revolutionary shock-resistant structure. The unique hollow case structure protected the movement from external shocks, and the urethane bezel provided an omni-directional buffer, keeping all the watch components safe.

The new G-SHOCK was not only praised by professionals working in extreme conditions; it also sparked a craze in youth culture, with skateboarders and others flocking to the brand. With the strength and functionality to handle hard use, all in a super-cool design, G-SHOCK watches have become a global favorite, an instantly recognizable must-have for street fashion, known for combining inspiration from sports, art, music, fashion, and other cultural forms. By 2017, more than 100 million G-SHOCK watches had been shipped worldwide.
Touchscreen calculator watch

Owners of this watch could perform calculator functions on the touchscreen. Just switch the LCD from timekeeping to calculator key display, then simply press the virtual keys shown on the screen with a fingertip on the glass to input math equations. With its large LCD set in a square case, the design previewed the smartwatches of today. The distinct look and feel of this model summed up the spirit of innovation behind every Casio watch.
First solar-powered Casio watch

The very first Casio solar watch, able to generate power from sunlight or even fluorescent lamps, combined a high-efficiency, amorphous silicon solar panel and an energy-efficient LSI developed by Casio. Power generated by the solar panel beneath the LCD ensured stable operation of various functions, while also recharging an internal battery to ensure smooth operation later in dark locations. Also offering 50-meter water resistance and a slim profile of just 6.5 mm, this design met all the demands of daily use.
Data Bank watches with telephone number storage

These Data Bank watches allowed users to store telephone numbers in internal memory. Ten combinations of numbers and letters (up to 12 numbers and 4 letters) could be stored for easy, on-the-spot recall. Also equipped with calculator functionality, this watch was handy for a wide range of settings, including business. As Data Bank functions continued to evolve, the name came to be synonymous with the multifunction digital watch.
Casio ships 100 millionth watch

Casio surpasses 100 million watches shipped, nine years and nine months after the November 1974 debut of the Casiotron. In less than a decade, Casio goes from the world’s first auto-calendar function to a wide array of other features, from calculator, dictionary, and phonebook functions to onboard thermometers and other sensors. The Casio focus on developing an information device to wear on the wrist is paying off, giving it a real presence in the watch market.
FS-10 (PELA)
Slim, lightweight digital watch with integrated case and band

This watch took a whole new approach to structure, creating a new fashion item befitting the digital age. The comprehensive design process started with the basic construction of the watch. Miniaturization technologies delivered dramatic size reductions, and hybrid molding techniques allowed for different materials to be molded together. The case and band were integrated — a revolutionary idea in wristwatch design. Featuring a slim profile at 3.9 mm and a light weight of just 12 g, this streamlined timepiece became an instant hit. Eventually, over one million were sold.
DBC-60, DBC-600
Data Bank watches with Telememo and schedule functions

These two watches came equipped with two special features for business users: a Telememo function that stored up to 50 telephone numbers, and a schedule function that provided reminders for up to 50 schedule items. The higher-capacity internal memory could store entries combining 5 letters and 12 numbers. These watches offered greater practical utility and expanded personalization options, as well, with auto-sort and secret functions for Telememo and an advance-notice feature for the schedule function that allowed users to check a two-week calendar for engagements and openings.
Twin-Graph watches with analog-style LCD

On these watches, the LCD was divided into digital and analog-style sections, incorporating practical watch features into a functional design. The clock in the analog-style window at the upper left displayed the time in hours and minutes, and the window at the upper right indicated seconds and also displayed graphics when in alarm, timer, and stopwatch modes. A pair of small and large digital displays showed the current time and could be used to check the month, date, and day of the week. Two models were offered: the AE-20 with a resin case, and the AE-200 with a stainless-steel case.
Sports watch with lap memory

The SDB-300W offered enhanced stopwatch functions to meet growing athletic demand, at a time when jogging, marathons, and triathlons were all the rage. The watch could do the lap/split time measurements essential for track races and had a memory function which stored up to 30 datapoints, each with a date. Other features useful for maintaining a steady pace during races, managing training, and more included average lap time calculation, target time alert, and timer functions.
Runner-oriented sports watch that checked pulse

This watch came equipped with a pulse-check function useful for training and health management. It used photoelectric pulse detection, employing LED light to measure changes in blood flow. Users simply placed a fingertip on the sensor to get a pulse readout. Comparing post-run readings with ordinary pulse rate could help users determine their optimal exercise intensity. Jogging-oriented features were incorporated as well, including a 1/100-second stopwatch, split time memory, and an electronic signal that helped runners keep their cadence and maintain their desired pace.
Watch that transmitted FM audio signals

The TM-100 was a highly unique wristwatch with the ability to transmit speech via radio. Outfitted with an FM transmitter and microphone, the watch allowed users to wirelessly broadcast their voice to a radio tuned to the right frequency simply by speaking toward the watch. This meant users could play their voice over a radio’s speakers. From using the watch outdoors as a wireless loudspeaker to recording conversations on a radio-cassette, this functionality opened the door to countless possibilities. Welcome the digital watch with a supremely playful, gadgety appeal.
Battery-less solar-powered watch

This watch made good use of the solar technology used for calculators and other devices in the 1980s. Goodbye, battery replacement! The power was stored in a capacitor to ensure stable operation of functions including the alarm and stopwatch. There was no doubt the watch was user-friendly, with features including quick start and charge indicator. The look of the watch made quite a splash by boldly incorporating functional elements into the design, for instance the large solar panel occupying a considerable portion of the watch face.
Watch with Phone Dialer function enabling audio-based dialing

Introducing Phone Dialer functionality. This new feature worked in tandem with the Telememo function, which stored up to 50 telephone numbers. Simply holding the watch’s built-in speaker up to the receiver of a push-button telephone allowed users to place calls to stored numbers, which were output in the form of touch-tone signals. At a time before mobile phones really hit the scene, this was an extremely revolutionary feature. Eliminating the need to manually dial numbers digit by digit while checking a telephone directory, people used it in a broad range of settings, including business.
Enduring standard captures the essence of the watch

This slim timepiece features a simple round dial that puts all the focus on the hour, minute, and seconds hands, for a watch that is easy to read and easy to use. The minimalist design conveys the essential function of a watch — telling the time — and embodies the pure aesthetic of pragmatic beauty. Great for men and women, young and old, casual and formal settings, the watch comes in a truly diverse range of design variations to meet individual needs.

Choose between bar index marks and numerals, and between conventional urethane, translucent, mesh, and other options for the band. Select classic black and white, or any number of colored dial variations—including metallic colors, matte hues, and earth tones. All kinds of people use the MQ-24 to express themselves — from those who choose a favorite watch and wear it for years, to those who like to switch up the color and look of their watch just like a change of clothes. A long-seller whose popularity has endured since 1987, the MQ-24 has won a loyal fan base including many celebrities and is still reaching new user segments today.
Simple, compact women’s watch

Combining practical functionality with fashion sensibility, this watch was specially designed with women in mind. Its compact size, meant to ensure a comfortable fit on slender wrists, and its minimalist form, suited to business and fun alike, have kept it popular for over 30 years. In 2011, it won the Long Life Design Award at the Good Design Awards in Japan. The design has stood the test of time. Today, it is attracting new admiration from younger users with little personal connection to the era when it first came out.

This watch comes in many design options, including metallic colors like silver and gold for the case, complemented by metal and leather band choices and a diverse variety of face colors. Fashion-conscious women just keep on choosing this watch.
Watch with a sensor for predicting weather patterns

Designed for outdoor sports enthusiasts, this timepiece could predict changes in weather. A pressure sensor automatically measured atmospheric pressure and displayed changes over an 18-hour span on a bar graph. Like a barometer on the wrist, the graph helped users know if the weather was likely to worsen or clear up. Measurements taken by the pressure sensor could also be used to calculate altitude and water depth — broadly useful functions for a range of activities, from mountain climbing to water sports.
Fitness watch with accelerometer

This watch came with features geared for exercise walking, helping people incorporate aerobic exercise into their health routines. In addition to a stopwatch for measuring time, the watch had an accelerometer to detect body movement and count steps. It also calculated calories burned after exercising based on the user’s data, including stride length, body weight, and age. It stored up to 30 datapoints in memory, for another handy feature for daily exercise management.
Cosmo Phase: 300 years of beautiful planetary orbits

The CGW-50 displayed the positions of the nine planets in our solar system (even the now-ousted Pluto!), along with Halley’s comet, for any given day in a 300-year period from 1901 to 2200, storing in memory their orbital paths around the sun. Simple button operation allowed users to enjoy scanning through the planets’ orbits at increased speed, as well as to view dates of the Halley’s comet’s closest approaches to Earth, total solar eclipses, and more. This very special digital watch had an outer space mystique that astronomy enthusiasts and watch fans of all ages loved.
The very definition of the digital watch

In the history of Casio watches, the F-91W takes its place as both the most memorable and a record-breaking bestseller. Ever since its launch in 1989, this watch has blazed a trail around the world, appearing on the wrists of the famous both in real life and on screen. Featuring a strong, slim, lightweight resin case, the watch is equipped with time and date display, stopwatch, alarm, and light functions. Easy to read, easy to use, easy to wear — this is a timepiece meticulously designed for quality down to the finest detail.

The F-91W has been joined by an extensive lineup with resin cases and bands and square designs. From the F-94W featuring a round indicator, to the W-59 with 50-meter water resistance, to the F-105W with EL backlight, each presented an evolution in form while maintaining the trademark multifunctionality of the F-91W. This line of timepieces demonstrates the Casio commitment to quality down to the tiniest details.
Digital watch with metal band

Equipped with the same movement as its peer, the F-91W, the A159W employs a metal band. The case features metallic color as well, to match the band. Crafted in Japan by the highly skilled engineers at Yamagata Casio, the watch is still sold around the world today, a long-selling favorite alongside the A158, which shares the same specs, but a different production location.
Digital watch with Map Meter function

The MAP-100 boasted a Map Meter function capable of calculating travel distances on paper maps. The watch was developed for the increasing number of people going for drives or camping on days off, capturing demand from the recreation boom of those days. Tracing a map route with the measurement roller on the watch’s bezel would display the actual distance based on the specified map scale. Travel time could be calculated as well, by inputting the speed of travel. This functionality was widely useful in a range of settings, from planning trips in advance at a time when digital maps were not yet widely available, to seeking the best route while out on the road.
